name: Lightbend, Inc. (formerly Typesafe; Akka)
subcategory: JVM reactive frameworks (Akka, Scala tooling, Play)
origin_detail: Founded in 2011 as Typesafe by Martin Odersky (creator of Scala at EPFL), Jonas Bonér (creator of Akka) and Paul Phillips to commercialize the Scala, Akka and Play stack; renamed Lightbend in 2016 and later rebranded around Akka (date unverified). Coded 'academic' because Scala came out of EPFL.
openness_notes: Scala, Akka and Play were Apache-2.0 and revenue came from subscriptions and support (3). In 2022 Akka moved to BSL 1.1 (converting to Apache-2.0 after three years), with fees for larger commercial users: level 1 for the flagship. Scala remains open under EPFL and Scala Center stewardship.

license_history.license: Apache-2.0 (Akka, Play; Scala BSD-style then Apache-2.0)

relicensing_events.outcome_note: Pekko entered the Apache Incubator soon after the change (unverified)

robustness: Akka is single-vendor under BSL, but the Apache-licensed lineage continues as Apache Pekko under ASF governance.
openness_effect_assessment: Not assessed: no sourced research was possible in this session.
key_takeaway: Draft only. Akka is the small-scale version of the HashiCorp story: a 2022 BSL switch quickly produced a foundation-governed fork (Apache Pekko), showing that even mid-sized ecosystems now fork into foundations.
